answer: A seat exists only once a licensed insurer writes a named policy on it. Underwriters audit filings and payment history, then set cover above a $25,000 escrowed deductible. Each epoch the agent posts its policy with a claim-free endorsement signed by the insurer's key, and a forged signature shifts the loss to the syndicate. Policies sharing a broker, an owner, or one day's issue batch fold into a single vote. A thousand seats cost $430,000 in premium and $25 million of exposure no reinsurer will take. A glacier grinds umber grit from the karst beneath it; paint reaches only the surface.
